questions.question: What does the 'Download' button on a lesson allow you to do?
options: It prints a physical copy of the lesson
It saves your current code to your computer so you can use it in your own IDE
It downloads a video of the lesson instructor
It clears all the code you have written
questions.explanation: The download button lets you take the Python code files from the platform and save them locally. This allows you to practice using your own professional tools.

questions.question: Besides a code editor, what must be installed on your computer to run Python code locally?
options: A premium subscription to a cloud service
questions.explanation: To run Python code on your computer, you must install the Python interpreter. Think of it as the 'engine' that translates your code into instructions the computer can follow.

questions.question: What is an IDE (Integrated Development Environment)?
options: A fast type of internet for developers
A special keyboard used for Python
Software for writing and testing code (like VS Code)
The part of the computer that stores your files
questions.explanation: An IDE like VS Code or PyCharm is a 'Dashboard' for developers. It combines a text editor with powerful tools like error detection and file management.

questions.question: Which of these is a benefit of using a local IDE instead of a simple browser editor?
options: Advanced features like real-time error detection and project management
It lets you play video games while you code
It automatically writes all of the code for you
questions.explanation: Local IDEs provide 'Power Tools' like real-time error detection (spotting bugs as you type) and the ability to manage projects with many different files.
